batching_note: NEITHER batching layer is exercised at this corpus tier, and no table may claim otherwise. chunk_text_blocks produces 4/3/4/3 chunks for AZ/CA/CO/TX against MAX_CHUNKS_PER_BATCH=5, so detection runs as exactly ONE batch per state (the Step Functions Map has a single iteration and merge_detection_batches merges one batch). Likewise the detector emits 2/3/3/2 domains against MAX_DOMAINS_PER_BATCH=3, so parsing is also a single batch per state. NV (5 chunks) and KY (3 chunks) are single-batch too. This is why the direct-vs-batched agreement measured here is close to structural rather than evidential, and why Task 6 (a full or _trimmed document) is required before any batching/scale claim.
caveats: CORPUS TIER: every number in this folder is from the _only_subset tier (8-15pp manually trimmed subset PDFs), never full documents.

THE DETECTOR SUITE'S RAW PRECISION IS ARITHMETICALLY ANNOTATION COVERAGE, NOT A HALLUCINATION RATE (guardrail 8, confirmed exactly this run): for CA, CO and TX the raw precision EQUALS the annotation-coverage ceiling to four decimal places (CA 0.2049 = 25/122, CO 0.1667 = 7/42, TX 0.3200 = 8/25), i.e. every unmatched in-scope detection is real unannotated document content and the metric carries zero information about detector correctness. AZ is the only state where the two differ (0.4167 vs 0.4545) and the gap is a scoping artifact, not a hallucination — see the fallback caveat below. All 7 AZ in-scope 'false positives' were inspected and are real AZ content (Strand 2 Relationships and Skills, Concepts 2 and 3, and indicators b-e under Concept 1). The paper's precision number comes from the Task 1b manual FP audit.

A GOLDEN MATCHED VIA THE DOMAIN-AGNOSTIC FALLBACK STILL COUNTS IN PRECISION'S NUMERATOR EVEN THOUGH ITS DETECTED COUNTERPART IS OUT OF SCOPE: AZ-IND-LL-1-2-b is annotated in the AZ golden without its Language-and-Literacy domain header, so the golden tags it to Social Emotional Development while the detection correctly places it in Language and Literacy. grade_elements pairs them through the domain-agnostic fallback, which adds 1 to `matched` without adding its detection to the in-scope pool, so AZ's precision denominator is 12 where the strictly-scoped count is 11. Effect: AZ raw precision 0.4167 instead of 0.3636. Zero effect on CA/CO/TX (0 fallback matches). Task 1b step 3 must resolve this AZ scoping quirk.

THE DOMAIN SCOPING DOES REAL WORK AND WAS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED: the match-path audit replays grade_elements' two-tier lookup and records which tier fired. All 25 CA goldens matched domain-scoped with 0 fallback, so the FLD/ELD same-titled Vocabulary and Grammar pairs were genuinely disambiguated by the enclosing domain rather than cross-matched. CO and TX likewise 0 fallback. AZ is 4 scoped + 1 fallback (the case above).

THE SUITE'S LEVEL-CONFUSION MATRIX IS STRUCTURALLY DIAGONAL: `level` is part of the match key in BOTH the domain-scoped and the domain-agnostic tier, so a level-misclassified element can never pair with its golden — it surfaces as one FN plus one FP instead. consolidate_task1.py computes the level-agnostic re-pairing that is what 'level confusion' actually means.

AGE-BAND DROPS CARRY NO INDEPENDENT SIGNAL WHEN RECALL IS 1.000: age_band_drops is a strict subset of missing_test_cases (a golden is only counted as an age-band drop if it went unmatched AND carried an age_band), so 'age-band drops: 0' follows arithmetically from recall 1.000 and is not a separate confirmation.

CODE AND DESCRIPTION ACCURACY ARE CONDITIONED ON THE TITLE ALREADY MATCHING EXACTLY: both are graded over MATCHED PAIRS ONLY, and matching requires an exact (case/whitespace-folded) title match. A garbled title removes that element from both denominators. This run the conditioning is vacuous because recall is 1.000 in every state, but the metric names do not say so and a future run with misses must report the denominator.

DESCRIPTION ACCURACY HAS A THIN DENOMINATOR: the goldens annotate a description on only 4/25 (AZ), 14/25 (CA), 4/7 (CO) and 3/8 (TX) elements; an unannotated element asserts nothing and is skipped. Report matches/total, never the bare rate.

THE GRADED DEPTH MAP IS NOT THE ONE THAT DROVE THE GRADED DETECTION: evaluate_state calls infer_depth_map a SECOND time purely for grading, after run_detector_cached has already called it once inside detect_structure. Two Haiku calls per state, and only the second is graded. This run they agreed for all four states (8 calls, 4 matching pairs — verified from the run log), so the risk did not materialize, but a PASS is not proof that the detection ran on a correct map. The call SHAPE is faithful to production: both detect_structure and detection_batching.prepare_detection_batches call infer_depth_map on the full block list, which samples ~6000 tokens internally.

PARSER FIELD ACCURACY AVERAGES OVER CELLS WHOSE GOLDEN IS NULL: 5.6% (AZ), 11.6% (CA), 22.2% (CO) and 16.7% (TX) of graded cells have an expected value of None — chiefly the three sub_strand.* cells per standard on a 3-level document. Those cells are not free (a spuriously invented sub_strand fails there, which is how the July depth-map regression showed itself), but 'field accuracy' and 'accuracy on the fields the golden asserts' are different numbers. summary.json reports both.
